4. Ms Mahfuza Begum, learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the applicant submits that the Tribunal was not justified in annulling the reassessment order of the DCT without considering the facts that the points dealt with in the reassessment order were different from those in the original assessment order and also in the consequential Tribunal's order. She also submits that the doctrine of merger is not applicable in this case because of the questions formulated in the reference application are not earlier decided by any authority below. In support of her submissions, learned Deputy Attorney-General referred to the case of The Commissioner of Taxes, Khulna Zone, Khulna vs M/s Reza Brothers, represented by Mr Rezaul Karim, reported in 1997 BTD 144 and one unreported case passed by this Division in Reference Application No.33 of 1995 (Md Ashraful Abedin-vs The Commissioner of Taxes). 

 12. The legal issue whether the assessment for the assessment year 1984-1985 is to be made under Income Tax Ordinance, 1984 or under the Income Tax Act, 1922 has been resolved in the case of The Commissioner of Taxes, Khulna Zone, Khulna vs M/s Reza Brothers, represented by Mr Rezaul Karim, reported in 1997 BTD 144.
